{{Article header|deck=A mapped region within a planetary ring that concentrates or identifies a named mining commodity.}}

{{Callout|type=tip|label=Quick answer|1=A '''mining hotspot''' helps target a named commodity, but it does not guarantee that every asteroid contains it or make every extraction method valid. Check the ring type, carry equipment for the intended method, and prospect individual asteroids after entering the hotspot.<ref name="hotspot">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Hotspot Hotspot], Elite Dangerous Wiki.</ref>}}

A '''mining hotspot''' is a persistent region within [[Planetary Rings|planetary rings]] associated with a named mined commodity. Mapping a ring with a [[Detailed Surface Scanner]] reveals its hotspot regions and their commodity labels.<ref name="hotspot" /><ref name="dss">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Detailed_Surface_Scanner Detailed Surface Scanner], Elite Dangerous Wiki.</ref>

Hotspots narrow a search; they do not replace the extraction method, a [[Prospector Limpet Controller|prospector limpet]], or the commodity distribution of the ring itself.

== Detection ==

A Detailed Surface Scanner probe fired into a ring reveals the ring's hotspot markers. Complex ring systems may have separate ring divisions, so make sure the probe strikes the division that will be mined.<ref name="dss" /> The complete scanning procedure is covered by [[How to Scan Planetary Rings for Mining Hotspots]].

The hotspot marker names the target commodity and shows the region's centre and extent. Entering closer to the centre is a targeting choice rather than a guarantee that the first asteroid will contain the named resource.

== Effect by mining method ==

=== Laser mining ===

For [[Laser Mining|laser mining]], current community testing treats a matching hotspot as the main way to improve the concentration of the target mineral. The system's reserve level also affects laser-mining yield, and the ring must support the commodity as a laser-mined resource.<ref name="edmining">[https://edmining.com/where-to-mine-in-elite-dangerous/ Where to Mine in Elite Dangerous], ED Mining.</ref>

A commodity label alone is therefore insufficient. For example, a Painite hotspot in a Metal Rich ring does not provide the same laser-mining route as a Painite hotspot in a Metallic ring; [[Painite]] documents the currently supported combinations.

=== Core mining ===

For [[Core Mining|core mining]], community testing indicates that hotspots increase the chance that a core contains the named commodity rather than increasing the total number of core asteroids. Core frequency is not treated as dependent on the system reserve level.<ref name="edmining" /> A commander must still locate core candidates and confirm the core resource with a prospector limpet.

=== Other asteroid methods ===

A hotspot does not guarantee that an asteroid has [[Sub-surface Mining|sub-surface deposits]] or [[Surface Deposit Mining|surface deposits]]. Those features must still be located and confirmed on individual asteroids. The commodity's reference article should be checked before assuming that the target can be extracted by either method.

== Overlap and depletion ==

Older routes often emphasise overlapping hotspot regions. Current community testing does not treat an overlap as automatically better than a suitable single hotspot for laser mining.<ref name="edmining" /> Exact hotspot strength and overlap formulas have not been published by Frontier, so route claims should be judged by current testing rather than the number of overlapping circles alone.

Mining can also leave individual asteroids or cores temporarily depleted. A busy hotspot may therefore produce a worse practical run than its label suggests, particularly for core mining where previously cracked asteroids remain unavailable until they replenish.<ref name="hotspot" /><ref name="edmining" />

== Planetary surface mining ==

Ring hotspots are not [[Surface Mining|Planetary Mining Locations]]. Planetary deposits are found from orbit with the Detailed Surface Scanner and worked on the ground with a [[Rhino]]; they use separate signals, equipment, and commodity distribution.

== Field Procedure ==

[[How to Scan Planetary Rings for Mining Hotspots]] explains how to probe the correct ring division, reveal its hotspots, and select a target marker.
